search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; lifetime-FWER fresh-audit gates; SeqE-Guard query-path design; finite-horizon evidence allocation; delayed/sparse-signal robustness

public_sources.title: Admissible online closed testing must employ e-values
public_sources.used_scope: SeqE-Guard maintains a product over queried candidates and unqueried e-values below 1; a true-discovery lower bound increments when the product reaches 1/alpha. The query path can be chosen online after observing the current e-value. This is the downstream multiple-testing interface used here; the new candidate-level e-value construction is worker-local.

public_sources.title: Learning to Bet for Horizon-Aware Anytime-Valid Testing
public_sources.authors: Ege Onur Taga; Samet Oymak; Shubhanshu Shekhar
public_sources.used_scope: Supports the general finite-horizon control principle: optimal anytime-valid betting depends on time and wealth, and more aggressive behavior can be optimal when behind schedule near a hard deadline. Used as conceptual support only; the exact tail-floor recurrence below is worker-local.

public_sources.author: Mark Von Tress

public_sources.used_scope: Supports fixing the number r of discordant matched pairs so the discordant signs have a fixed exact-binomial sample size while total paired-task cost is random/negative-binomial.

public_sources.title: Improving online FDR procedures via online analogs of e-closure and compound e-values
public_sources.authors: Ziyu Xu; Lasse Fischer; Aaditya Ramdas
public_sources.used_scope: Background only for the next frontier: online e-closure/donation can strictly improve some online e-value procedures and explicitly targets adaptively generated hypothesis streams, including LLM-agent settings. It controls FDR/SupFDR, not the lifetime-FWER commit gate derived here.

two_level_tail_floor_candidate_evalue.setup: After inverse sampling to r discordant pairs, let W be candidate-only wins. Under the equality null W~Binomial(r,1/2). Let C be SeqE-Guard's current off-query product from prior unqueried e-values below 1 and m=1/(alpha*C). For a deterministic upper-tail rejection set A_k={W>=k}, let p_k=P0(A_k) and require m*p_k<1.
two_level_tail_floor_candidate_evalue.construction: Define c_k=(1-m*p_k)/(1-p_k), and define G_k(W)=m on A_k and c_k on its complement. Then E0[G_k]=1 exactly and 0<c_k<=1. If W is in A_k, query the candidate and C*G_k=1/alpha so the strict SeqE-Guard lower bound increments. Otherwise leave the candidate unqueried; G_k=c_k<1 enters U and the next product is C<-C*c_k, equivalently m<-m/c_k.
two_level_tail_floor_candidate_evalue.important_difference_from_prior_boosting: This redesign is not constrained to pointwise increase the previous likelihood-ratio e-value. Mid-range e-values that would be >1 but insufficient to commit are deliberately collapsed toward the complement floor, because values in (1,m) consume null expectation without improving either immediate strict-commit status or future U-product wealth.
two_level_tail_floor_candidate_evalue.scope_guard: Validity requires the candidate to be frozen before the fresh audit and the emitted candidate-level e-value to remain conditionally valid given the prior stream. The construction uses the fixed-discordant Binomial(r,1/2) null; it does not justify reuse of adaptive development data as fresh audit data.

fixed_rejection_set_log_wealth_optimalit.result: For a fixed current commit set A and threshold m, setting commit outcomes exactly to m is budget-minimal. Any noncommit value above 1 can be replaced by 1 without worsening the strict query path. On the complement, after fixing the remaining null expectation budget, Jensen's inequality makes a constant floor c maximize null expected log(min(G,1)). Therefore the two-level {m,c} form is optimal for preserving null-prefix log wealth among maps with the same commit set. For Binomial(r,q), q>1/2 versus Binomial(r,1/2), the monotone likelihood ratio makes an upper tail A_k the Neyman-Pearson choice for current alternative commit probability at a given null tail mass.
fixed_rejection_set_log_wealth_optimalit.interpretation: The previous high-dimensional boost-map search collapses to a one-dimensional choice of k when the utility is current commit power plus null-prefix wealth preservation.

discreteness_slack_is_future_wealth.result: For a single test, boundary randomization can spend discrete size slack to approach the exact level. In a repeated strict-commit stream, that same slack can instead be converted into c_k close to 1 and carried forward as future e-wealth. At m=20, randomizing the k=15 boundary all the way to null rejection probability .05 would exhaust the expectation budget and leave zero complement floor in the two-level representation, destroying future evidence after a nonrejection. Thus single-test power-optimal randomization need not be stream-utility optimal.

finite_horizon_tail_choice_recurrence.model: For a pre-audit predictive prior pi that the current frozen candidate is genuinely improved, good discordant signs are Binomial(r,q_good), null signs are Binomial(r,1/2), and a false commit is terminal failure while a true commit is terminal success.
finite_horizon_tail_choice_recurrence.recurrence: V_n(m)=max_k [pi*q_k + {pi*(1-q_k)+(1-pi)*(1-p_k)}*V_{n-1}(m/c_k)], over valid k plus a no-test action, with V_0=0.
finite_horizon_tail_choice_recurrence.observed_policy_r20_q075_H20: On the tested log-m grid, pi in {0.05,0.10,0.20,0.30,0.40} produced the same survival-path action pattern to numerical resolution: k=17 for approximately the first 15 opportunities, then k=16 for the final 5. This uses conservative tails early to preserve product wealth and spends more remaining risk near the horizon.
finite_horizon_tail_choice_recurrence.scope_guard: This is an approximate finite-grid Bellman solution under a stylized fixed q_good and prior. The e-validity of every chosen map does not depend on the prior being correct, but the power optimality does.

worker_local_stress_tests.common: Exact probability calculations unless explicitly marked Monte Carlo. alpha=.05; strict SeqE-Guard commit query; r=20 fixed discordant signs per launched audit; good sign probability q=.75; null sign probability .5. The Bellman-tail-floor path is approximated by k=17 for the first 15 surviving candidate opportunities and k=16 for the final 5, with c_k recomputed from current m each time.

timing_patterns.comparison_to_prior_frozen_checkpoint: The prior scalar/floor product boosts were stronger for front-loaded five-good candidates (about .951/.906 true-commit) but had zero observed true commits for five-good positions 11-15 in 100k runs; floor boost was about .0206 on the sparse 5/10/15/20 pattern. The new tail-floor horizon policy spends much more of the nominal FWER budget but removes most timing collapse in these tested patterns.

all_five_of_twenty_placements.interpretation: The horizon spend mainly raises median/best placement power while preserving nearly the same worst-placement true-commit probability as a fixed k=17 rule; it uses the additional global risk budget late in the horizon.

clustered_proposal_stream_100000.proposal_process: 30 proposal opportunities; hot/cold Markov state with P(hot|hot)=.85 and P(hot|cold)=.15, initial hot=.5; P(good|hot)=.65 and P(good|cold)=.10; development-only triage launches .80 of good and .25 of null proposals; cap 20 launched audits. Candidate-quality/launch streams were Monte Carlo sampled; conditional audit commit probabilities were integrated analytically rather than sampling W.
clustered_proposal_stream_100000.comparison_to_prior_frozen_checkpoint: Under the same stylized proposal process, prior floor/scalar product boosts reported about .667/.601 probability of any true commit. The new policy is materially stronger in this tested clustered regime, while its all-null risk is closer to the full .05 budget.

worker_local_stress_tests.cost_interpretation: Larger r can lower expected total paired observations when improvements arrive early because a successful candidate terminates after very few launched audits, but it greatly increases all-null and late-signal cost. Therefore r itself should be a horizon/timing-aware control variable rather than a fixed notion of statistical quality.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Turn each fixed-discordant exact-binomial audit into a two-level candidate e-value: current SeqE-Guard threshold m on a most-powerful upper tail and a constant complement floor carrying unused discrete null budget forward.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Exact null-expectation derivation plus exhaustive 5-of-20 timing calculations and clustered-stream stress test.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires conditionally fresh candidate audits and fixed-discordant sign symmetry; does not repair adaptive reuse bias. Uses more of the global false-commit budget than prior conservative boosts.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Choose the tail threshold as a predictable function of remaining horizon and current off-query wealth, conservative early and more aggressive near deadline.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Finite-grid Bellman recurrence and exact r=20 timing enumeration; tested survival path approximately k17 for 15 opportunities then k16 for 5.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Power optimality depends on the stylized alternative/prior; validity does not. Needs robust/minimax calibration before operational recommendation.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat fixed discordant count r as a decision variable jointly with tail threshold; larger r is cheap when true improvements arrive early but expensive under long null prefixes or late improvements.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: r=10/20/30/50 exact power plus expected inverse-sampling cost calculations at discordance rho=.4.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Expected cost uses a fixed rho=.4 and ignores wall-clock/tool parallelism; low-rho tails can be much worse.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'pointwise e-value boosting is the only safe way to improve SeqE-Guard power.' A candidate-level e-value may be redesigned from its fresh sufficient statistic as long as conditional null expectation is <=1; deliberately shrinking non-decision-relevant mid-range values can preserve future query-path wealth.

Rejected: 'single-test exact-level randomization is automatically best in a repeated commit stream.' Spending all discrete slack on the current boundary can erase the complement floor and harm future opportunities.

Rejected: 'using nearly the full FWER budget early maximizes lifetime power.' k15/k16 are excellent for front-loaded improvements but exhibit severe late-signal collapse despite all-null FWER remaining near .05.

Narrowed: 'floor boosting cannot solve delayed signals.' A floor-only transform of a fixed raw e-value was insufficient, but a coupled rejection-tail plus floor redesign can remove most tested timing collapse by changing where null expectation is spent.

Narrowed: 'larger r is always more expensive.' Under early strong improvements, r=30-50 can reduce expected total paired observations through much faster termination; under all-null/late regimes it is substantially more expensive.

frontier.action: Solve a robust/minimax version of the tail-floor horizon policy over uncertain q_good and candidate-timing distributions. Compare fixed k17, 15xk17+5xk16, prior-weighted Bellman, and a least-favorable timing/effect mixture while keeping each emitted e-value conditionally valid.

Jointly optimize discordant depth r and tail threshold k under a total paired-task budget. Allow r to vary predictably by horizon/wealth and derive whether switching from cheap r=10 scanning to deeper r=30 confirmation dominates fixed r. Include rho uncertainty and negative-binomial tail risk, not only mean cost.

Formalize the dynamic value of discrete nonrandomization: compare deterministic slack-recycling tail-floor, boundary-randomized exact tests, raw likelihood-ratio e-values, and query-path boosts under identical lifetime-FWER and deadline utility. Derive when spending size slack now versus carrying it as e-wealth is optimal.

Remove inverse-sampling's random total cost by constructing fixed-total/censored paired audits that emit a conditionally valid candidate e-value with an analogous tail-floor decomposition uniformly over unknown discordance rate, or prove a meaningful impossibility/lower bound.

Inspect whether 2026 online compound-e-value/donation constructions can be adapted to the lifetime-FWER strict-commit objective without weakening to FDR/SupFDR; keep candidate-freeze/fresh-audit validity separate from multiplicity power.

exact_next_action: Derive a least-favorable/minimax tail-floor policy for 20 candidate opportunities with q_good in [0.60,0.80] and unknown placement of 1-5 true improvements, then compare worst-case true-commit probability and all-null FWER against fixed k17 and the 15xk17+5xk16 horizon-spend schedule.
